workflows.description: Instructors create and manage quizzes, questions, and answers through a web interface. This involves dynamic form loading, content editing, and persistence to the Quiz Service.
Students start, attempt, and submit quizzes. This workflow handles time limits, deadlines, attempts tracking, partial submission saving, and proctoring integration.
Students view their submitted quiz results, including scores, historical attempts, and proctoring status. This workflow supports navigation between different submissions.
Students can view a detailed recap of quiz questions and their answers, often used for review or learning purposes.

Administrators perform various regrading operations on quizzes, questions, or answers, typically via command-line `rake` tasks on the Quiz Service. This allows for adjustments to scores after quiz content changes or errors.
Users log in to the platform using various external identity providers (e.g., SAML, OpenID Connect) configured through OmniAuth.
Users view and update their personal information, including custom fields and consent preferences, on their profile page.
External applications or services authenticate with the Portal API using OAuth 2.0 Bearer Tokens to access platform resources.
Administrators define and assign roles and groups to control access and permissions for users within the `Xikolo Account Service` and potentially other parts of the platform.

Teachers create, edit, organize, and delete course sections and various content items (rich text, video, quiz, LTI exercise). This workflow involves frontend forms, backend controllers, and microservice interactions for data persistence and file management.

Learners enroll in courses, potentially through a launch page, and can reactivate past courses. The system handles various enrollment scenarios, including invite-only courses and prerequisite checks, and provides appropriate feedback and redirects.

Learners view their overall course progress, access the course syllabus, and navigate through individual content items. The system tracks item visits and displays item status (locked, visited, active) and time effort.
Users can view course documents, while teachers can perform CRUD operations on documents and their localizations. This includes uploading document files to S3 and associating them with courses.

Administrators create, edit, and list general announcements, distinguishing between drafts and published items. This workflow primarily uses the `Admin::AnnouncementsController` and `Admin::AnnouncementForm`.

Administrators compose and send announcement emails to selected recipients (users, courses, groups). This involves selecting recipients, defining email content, and triggering the send via the NewsService.
Administrators create, edit, and delete news items (homepage announcements), which can include visual media and audience targeting. This workflow also allows sending associated emails.
Users view published announcements and news items on the application's homepage. Privileged users may also see unpublished drafts.
The system tracks when users view announcements, asynchronously notifying the NewsService to mark them as read.
Users can browse discussions for a course, filter by sections (including a special 'Technical Issues' section) or tags, and create new questions. Course administrators can manage tags.
Users can create, view, edit, and delete questions, answers, and comments. This includes features like upvoting questions/answers, accepting an answer for a question, and subscribing to questions.

Users can report questions, answers, or comments for abuse. Authorized moderators can block or unblock any pinboard entity (question, answer, comment) and delete questions or comments. They can also close/reopen questions.

User actions on the pinboard (e.g., posting, answering, commenting) contribute to their gamification scores. These scores are used to display user states/levels next to their posts, if the gamification feature is enabled.
Allows users to disable specific email notification types directly from an email link without logging in. This involves validating the request and updating user preferences in the Account service.
Handles the end-to-end process of sending an email notification, from receiving an event to rendering, styling, tracking, and dispatching the email.

The process of dynamically generating the administrative dashboard's navigation menu. This workflow involves checking the current user's permissions and system-wide feature flags to determine which menu items are visible and accessible.

The manual, console-based process of granting or revoking the `lanalytics.report.admin` role to users. This workflow is critical due to the sensitive nature of the data involved and bypasses UI-driven administration for enhanced control and policy adherence.

A client (e.g., mobile app) sends a request to the `/api` endpoint. The request includes an `Accept` header specifying the desired API version. The `Xikolo::API` (Grape application) processes the request, potentially authenticating it, and fetches/stores data from backend services. The response adheres to JSON-API and includes the actual API version and potentially a `Sunset` header for deprecation notices.

An external client (e.g., customer portal) sends a request to the `/portalapi-beta` endpoint. The request must include an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header for authentication and an `Accept` header for version negotiation. The `Xi::Controllers::RequireBearerToken` middleware validates the token. If valid, the request is routed to the `PortalApi` module's controllers, which process the request and return a JSON-API compliant response, potentially with `application/problem+json` for errors.

Internal or specific external systems send requests to various `/bridges` sub-endpoints (e.g., `/bridges/chatbot/authenticate`). These requests are routed to the respective `Bridges` sub-modules (e.g., `Chatbot` module). Authentication and data formats may vary depending on the specific bridge, but they generally facilitate inter-service communication or specialized integrations.

A client sends an API request with an `Accept` header containing `xikolo-version=<client_version>`. The API determines the latest compatible minor version and responds with `Content-Type` including `xikolo-version=<server_version>`. If the client's version is deprecated, the response also includes a `Sunset` header with an expiration date.

An API client includes an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header in its request. The `Xi::Controllers::RequireBearerToken` middleware intercepts the request, extracts the token, and compares it against a configured secret. If the token is missing or invalid, the middleware immediately terminates the request with a `401 Unauthorized` HTTP Problem Details response and a `WWW-Authenticate` header.
The process of compiling, bundling, and optimizing JavaScript, TypeScript, and Sass assets into deployable bundles for the web application.
The workflow for rendering dynamic and interactive user interfaces directly in the user's browser using modern JavaScript frameworks and libraries.
The process of composing and rendering reusable UI components on the server using Ruby, which are then delivered as HTML to the client.
The workflow for maintaining consistent code style and adherence to best practices across Ruby, Slim, JavaScript/TypeScript, and SCSS codebases using static analysis and formatting tools.
The process of adding, updating, and managing external JavaScript and CSS libraries and tools required for frontend development and deployment.

workflows.workflowName: User Earns Gamification Points and Badges
workflows.description: A user performs an action (e.g., takes an exam, answers a question, visits a course item) which triggers an event. This event is consumed by the `GamificationConsumer`, which then dispatches to a specific `Gamification::Rules` class to calculate and record points. These accumulated points contribute towards achieving different levels of badges as defined in `Gamification::BadgeTypes`.

A logged-in user navigates to the dashboard achievements page. The system retrieves the user's earned badges and scores. Each badge is rendered by the `Dashboard::GamificationBadge` component, displaying its image and title. The user's total points and course-specific XP are also displayed, provided the gamification feature is enabled.
Administrators create, update, and delete templates for certificates and Open Badges within a specific course. This involves uploading PDF or PNG files and configuring template-specific metadata.

Authenticated users can view their earned certificates and Open Badges for a course, and download official PDF certificates. This workflow includes checks for course eligibility and proctoring status for certificate downloads.
Any user can verify the authenticity of an issued certificate by providing its unique verification code. The system displays the certificate details and, if applicable, the associated Open Badge.

(Intended) After a user completes a proctored quiz, a background job is triggered to fetch their proctoring image from the SMOWL service and store it in S3, making it available for inclusion in their certificates.
Administrators create, edit, and delete global LTI providers through a dedicated admin interface. This workflow includes form submission, validation, and handling of privacy settings.

Course administrators manage LTI providers that are scoped to a particular course. This involves creating, updating, and deleting LTI provider configurations within the context of a course, with specific permissions for privacy settings.
A user initiates an LTI tool from a course item. The system determines the display method (intro page or iframe), prepares the LTI launch request, and redirects or embeds the external tool.
An external LTI tool sends a grading callback to the platform. The system validates the request, processes the grade, publishes analytics events, and responds to the LTI tool.
After an LTI grade is received and recorded, a background job is initiated to publish this grade to the course service, ensuring it is accounted for in the user's course progress.
The process of creating or updating the content, specifically instructions, for an LTI exercise. This includes handling embedded S3 file uploads and managing their lifecycle.

An administrator views a course item's time effort, which can be a calculated value or a previously overwritten value. The administrator then manually enters a new time effort, overriding any calculated value.

An administrator, after viewing or overwriting a course item's time effort, chooses to remove the manual override. The system then reverts to displaying the automatically calculated time effort for that item.

The process of starting the Rails application, loading gems, configuring environment settings, and initializing middleware. This includes conditional loading of `bootsnap` for development speed and setting up core Rails configurations.

The process by which the application loads and manages its various settings from YAML files and environment variables. This involves a hierarchical loading order, allowing for environment-specific overrides and centralized management of platform features and integrations.
The process of compiling, precompiling, and serving frontend assets (JavaScript, CSS, images). This includes internationalization exports for JavaScript and brand-specific asset checks.

The mechanism for offloading long-running or asynchronous tasks, such as sending emails or executing scheduled maintenance, to background workers. This involves using Delayed Job for Active Job and Sidekiq for more complex job management and cron-based scheduling.

A workflow for setting up the application environment specifically for Continuous Integration (CI) pipelines. This involves exporting i18n assets, dropping and recreating databases, and loading the schema.
The process of setting up a local development environment using Docker Compose, providing essential services like PostgreSQL, Minio (S3), RabbitMQ, and Redis for local development and testing.

This workflow involves services publishing events related to user activity (e.g., pinboard interactions, course completions) to RabbitMQ. The main application's GamificationController subscribes to these events and processes them to award experience points or trigger other gamification logic.
Administrators can add, edit, update, and delete video providers, configuring their credentials. They can also trigger full or partial synchronizations of videos from these providers.

Teachers or administrators can upload and associate various digital assets (slides, transcripts, reading material) and subtitles with a video. The system handles storage, processing, and linking of these assets.

Users can stream video content, with the system dynamically generating HLS playlists tailored to bandwidth and integrating available subtitles. The client-side player provides interactive features like timestamp seeking and keyboard shortcuts.

Authenticated users can download video streams in different qualities, provided the course settings allow it. The system generates secure download links and handles various availability and quality-related errors.

Users can create discussion topics directly linked to specific timestamps within a video, fostering contextual conversations. These topics are displayed alongside the video, allowing for easy navigation to relevant video segments.
An external translation pipeline (Transpipe) can query course and video metadata, including stream URLs and subtitle content, via a dedicated API. It also allows for updating subtitle content.
This workflow manages the execution of recurring tasks at predefined intervals using cron expressions. Jobs are defined as ActiveJobs and processed by the configured background job system.

This workflow handles the execution of various jobs asynchronously in the background, offloading work from the main application thread. It includes managing job queues, retries, and execution limits, with integrated monitoring.

workflows.workflowName: Chatbot User Interaction and Course Management
workflows.description: An external chatbot system authenticates users, retrieves their profile and course information, and enables them to enroll in or unenroll from courses, as well as check their achievements and quizzes. This workflow relies on a two-step authentication process: a shared secret for initial token generation, followed by user-specific PASETO tokens for subsequent interactions.

External shop systems can programmatically create multiple vouchers for various platform products (e.g., course reactivation, proctoring) and list existing vouchers, optionally filtering by status or date. This enables third-party sales channels to integrate directly with the platform's voucher system.

The platform exposes course data to the MOOChub system, adhering to the MOOChub Schema. This workflow facilitates data exchange and potential synchronization of course information with the MOOChub ecosystem.

The translation pipeline (TransPipe) retrieves comprehensive course and video details, including their structure and available streams. It also manages video subtitles by retrieving existing VTT files and allowing updates or creation of new subtitles for specific languages.

Users with appropriate permissions can view aggregated statistics across the entire platform, including user counts, enrollment trends, and overall activity. Data is fetched concurrently from multiple microservices and cached.

Administrators can access detailed analytics for individual courses, covering geographical distribution of learners, item engagement, video consumption, and pinboard activity. Data is fetched from various microservices and cached.

Authorized users can create, monitor, restart, and delete custom data reports. The system fetches available report types and their configurable options, then dispatches report generation jobs to an external analytics service. Permissions are strictly enforced.

The core application calculates and provides various statistics directly on `Course` objects, such as enrollment figures, user engagement (shows), and certificate attainment, often leveraging cached data and external analytics services.
A user submits a helpdesk ticket via the web interface. The submission is validated, a ticket record is created, and subsequent notifications and messaging events are triggered.

An external system or client application submits a helpdesk ticket programmatically via the API. The API endpoint validates the request, creates a ticket record, and triggers notifications and messaging events.

After a helpdesk ticket is created (either via frontend or API), an email notification is sent to the helpdesk, and a message is published to RabbitMQ for asynchronous processing by other integrated systems.
Administrators create batches of vouchers through a web interface, specifying the quantity and attributes. This process leverages a service object for the actual voucher generation.
External shop systems programmatically create batches of vouchers by calling a dedicated API endpoint. This enables automated voucher generation as part of a sales or marketing process.

Authenticated users redeem a voucher code on a course details page to activate a specific product for that course. The process involves multiple validations, claiming the voucher, and activating the product atomically.
Administrators can query individual vouchers and view statistics, while external shops can list created vouchers, filtered by various criteria, to verify their status and redemption details.
A daily background job automatically clears claimant IP addresses from redeemed vouchers after one year to comply with data privacy regulations.
The process of compiling legacy JavaScript assets using Sprockets, primarily for jQuery and Bootstrap dependencies. This is a transitional workflow as the project moves to Webpack.
The modern process of compiling JavaScript and SCSS assets using Webpack. This workflow integrates polyfills, Rails UJS, and a modular structure for UI components and utilities.

The core workflow for user authentication, session management, and permission checks across the application. This includes handling login, logout, and ensuring users have the necessary privileges for actions.
The workflow for displaying and managing static content pages, including translations and file uploads. This involves fetching pages for display and providing an administrative interface for editing.

The process of rendering various reusable UI components that provide consistent user interface elements and interactions across the application. This includes accordions, dropdowns, tooltips, and flash messages.
The workflow for catching, logging, and displaying application errors to users, including custom error pages and integration with monitoring tools.
The workflow for rendering and sanitizing Markdown content, ensuring proper display and security against XSS vulnerabilities, and handling special link behaviors.

When an unhandled exception occurs in the application, Sentry captures it. Sensitive parameters are filtered, and common, expected exceptions are ignored. The `AnnotateSentryErrorsForMnemosyne` middleware ensures that the current Mnemosyne trace ID is added to the Sentry event for cross-system correlation, allowing developers to link errors to their performance context.

Sentry and Mnemosyne work in conjunction to collect performance data for requests and background jobs. Sentry samples transactions based on configured rates and rules (e.g., ignoring health checks). Mnemosyne collects detailed distributed traces, which are then sent to a RabbitMQ instance via AMQP for further analysis.

Application code can emit custom metrics (e.g., counters, gauges) using the `Xikolo.metrics` interface. These metrics are sent via UDP to a local Telegraf agent, which is responsible for aggregating and forwarding them to a time-series database for visualization and alerting.

This workflow describes how the form for creating and editing course items (app/views/items/_form.html.slim) dynamically adjusts its visible inputs and content based on the selected content_type (e.g., quiz, video) and other specific attributes like exercise_type. Frontend JavaScript (form.ts) handles the toggling of visibility and appending of relevant form templates.
The process of running automated tests for Ruby code and generating code coverage reports to ensure code quality and identify untested areas.
The process of setting up a new development environment or updating an existing one, including dependency management, database setup, and system cleanup.

The process of setting up a new database instance, applying the latest schema definition, enabling necessary PostgreSQL extensions, defining custom functions and enums, and populating it with initial seed data for development or testing environments.

The ongoing process of modifying the database schema and data in a controlled, incremental manner using Rails migrations. This workflow emphasizes best practices for performance, reversibility, and a structured approach to data transformations, including specific steps for migrating data to new resources.

The system-wide strategy for uniquely identifying resources using UUIDs. This includes the generation of time-ordered UUIDv7 as primary keys in the database and their conversion to URL-friendly base62 strings for application-level parameter handling.
External systems can retrieve a list of all publicly visible courses or detailed information for a specific course.
External systems can update specific attributes of a user's profile (e.g., email, name, language) or delete a user account.
External systems can retrieve a user's enrollments (either all or for a specific course) and create new enrollments for a user in a given course.

This workflow describes the steps required to enable and configure the proctoring feature at both the platform and individual course levels. It involves setting up external shop URLs, SMOWL API credentials, proctoring thresholds, and activating the feature via a feature flipper and course administration settings.

This workflow covers the process where a user attempts to obtain proctored status for a course, typically by redeeming a voucher. It includes checks for global and course-specific proctoring enablement, user enrollment status, and existing proctored status, culminating in an API call to update the enrollment.

This workflow describes how proctoring-related data, such as images or results, are handled and stored. It involves generating unique identifiers for storage paths and processing vendor-specific data from quiz submissions.

This workflow outlines how proctoring results are presented to users or administrators in the application's UI. It involves interpreting raw proctoring data and rendering it in a human-readable format, including status callouts and visual charts.
Handles general background tasks initiated via ActiveJob, processed by `Delayed::Worker` across defined queues. Includes monitoring of job execution and failures.
Manages the execution of periodic tasks defined in `config/cron.yml` using `Sidekiq` and `sidekiq-cron`. Examples include data cleanup and synchronization tasks.
Processes incoming RabbitMQ messages from various services, routing them to specific internal consumers to trigger actions, particularly for gamification events.

The process of consistently generating URLs and asset paths across the main web application. This ensures that all links and resource references are correctly formed, taking into account the application's base URL configuration.

When a user clicks an external link within the application, this workflow ensures a safe redirection by validating the target URL and optionally displaying an interstitial notice. This prevents open redirect vulnerabilities.

workflows.workflowName: Deep Linking and App Link Verification
workflows.description: This workflow enables deep linking from mobile applications to specific content within the Xikolo platform, supporting both iOS Universal Links and Android Digital Asset Links. It involves serving `.well-known` files with specific configurations.

Handles various specialized redirection needs, such as launching courses, navigating to specific items or pinboard discussions, and forwarding users to external survey platforms like LimeSurvey, often involving inter-service communication to retrieve necessary data.

Each microservice defines its own set of API endpoints, primarily for internal communication or specific external integrations. This workflow describes how requests are routed and handled within each service to provide JSON-based responses.

Administrators create, view, edit, and delete documents. This involves interacting with the `Admin::DocumentsController` in the main web application, which then communicates with the `Document` model in the `Xikolo::Course` microservice. File uploads are handled via `DocumentHelper` and the `xikolo-s3` gem.

Administrators create, view, edit, and delete localized versions of documents. This workflow is managed by the `Admin::DocumentLocalizationsController`, which interacts with the `DocumentLocalization` model in the `Xikolo::Course` microservice. File uploads for localized documents are handled through `DocumentHelper` and the `xikolo-s3` gem.

Users view documents associated with a specific course. The `Course::DocumentsController` in the main web application fetches relevant documents from the `Xikolo::Course` microservice API and displays them to the user, ensuring the user is logged in and within the correct course context.

Files for documents and document localizations are uploaded to a temporary S3 bucket, validated, and then copied to their final S3 destination. This process is orchestrated by `DocumentHelper` in the frontend and handled by `Xikolo::S3::UploadByUri` or `Xikolo::S3::TextWithUploadsProcessor` in the backend, ensuring correct metadata (`xikolo-state`, `xikolo-purpose`) and S3 key generation.
A user views the main page for a course, seeing general information, teachers, sections, and featured items.
A user navigates to the course syllabus to see an overview of all content and their progress.
A user views a specific learning item within a course, potentially encountering prerequisites or recording a visit.
A content editor creates, updates, moves, or deletes sections within a course.
A content editor creates, updates, moves, or deletes learning items within a course section.
A user or administrator views the progress of a learner in a course, seeing metrics and item statuses.

A new user registers for the platform, providing personal details and consenting to required and optional data treatments. The system then sends a confirmation email and, upon confirmation, allows the user to log in.
Users authenticate to the platform using either their registered email and password or via a Single Sign-On (SSO) provider. The system handles session management, redirects, and policy acceptance.
Logged-in users can view and update their personal information, email addresses, linked external accounts, custom profile fields, and avatar image.
Users can review and modify their consent preferences for various data treatments on their profile page. The system updates their consent status and associated memberships.
Users who have forgotten their password can request a reset. The system sends a unique link to their email, allowing them to set a new password.
Users can configure their platform preferences, such as email notification settings and UI behaviors.
Describes the process of rendering a web page in the Xikolo application, from controller action to final HTML output, integrating layouts, ViewComponents, and frontend assets.

workflows.workflowName: Frontend Asset Compilation and Serving Workflow
workflows.description: Details how JavaScript and SCSS assets are processed, bundled, and served to the client, highlighting the hybrid approach using both Sprockets and Webpack.
Describes how user actions on the frontend trigger JavaScript code, which then manipulates the DOM or communicates with the backend, supported by global UI components and form actions.
Platform administrators define and organize classifiers and their clusters through a web interface, which are then used to tag and filter courses for end-users.
Administrators or integrated external shop systems create vouchers, either via a self-service UI or an API, that users can later redeem to activate paid features for courses.

Administrators manually assign or remove the `lanalytics.report.admin` role to specific users using the Rails console within the `xi-account` service, granting or revoking access to sensitive reporting data.
Allows users to launch external LTI tools from an LTI exercise item within a course, potentially displaying an introductory page or embedding the tool directly.
Processes grade submissions from external LTI tools, including validation, score persistence, and publishing analytics events.
Asynchronously publishes recorded LTI grades to the course service to update user progress and other internal systems.
Enables authorized users (administrators) to create, view, update, and delete LTI provider configurations for courses, including managing privacy settings.

When a user accesses their dashboard achievements page, a `Gamification` presenter/decorator aggregates their earned badges and scores. The `achievements.html.slim` view then renders this data, utilizing the `Dashboard::GamificationBadge` component for individual badge representation and a table for displaying scores, or a `State::Empty` component if no scores exist.

Gamification badges are defined through the `Gamification Badge Configuration` (`badge_types.yml`), which specifies the rules that contribute to each badge and the score thresholds for achieving various levels. As users accumulate scores from relevant events processed by `Gamification::Rules`, they progress through the levels of applicable badges.

User levels are configured in the `Gamification User Level Configuration` (`user_levels.yml`), mapping accumulated experience points (XP) to specific level titles and associated imagery. As users gain XP through various gamified actions, their overall user level is determined based on these thresholds.
Content editors create, edit, update, reorder, and delete quiz questions and their associated answers within a course item. This workflow ensures the integrity of quiz content.

A learner initiates a quiz, potentially saves intermediate progress, and finally submits their answers. The system validates deadlines, time limits, and processes the submission, publishing an event upon completion.
After submitting a quiz, a learner can review their submission, view results, and see a recap of questions. They can also navigate through past submissions.
A user navigates to the pinboard index for a course, potentially filtering by sections or tags. The system fetches and displays a list of questions.
A user clicks on a specific question to view its details, including the question text, answers, comments, and related metadata. The system also tracks question reads for analytics.
A user creates a new question, answer, or comment. The system validates the input, persists the data via the Pinboard microservice, and handles notifications.

workflows.workflowName: Moderate Pinboard Content (Edit, Delete, Block, Unblock, Close, Reopen)
workflows.description: Authorized users (e.g., instructors or administrators) can edit, delete, block, unblock, close, or reopen questions and comments. The system performs authorization checks and updates the content status.
Users can report questions or comments for abuse. The system records the report and provides feedback to the user.
Logged-in users can upvote questions or answers. The system records the vote and updates the vote count.
The author of a question can accept one of the answers. This action marks the answer as accepted and publishes an event for analytics.

This workflow describes how video content, including various quality streams, subtitles, and supplementary materials, is delivered to the user for playback or download. It involves dynamic HLS playlist generation and direct file serving.
This workflow enables custom styling for the Google Chromecast Styled Media Receiver (SMR) based on Xikolo's configuration, allowing for branded casting experiences.
This workflow facilitates the generation of specific URLs for courses and videos that are intended for consumption or processing by an external 'Transpipe' service, if enabled.

An incoming API request is received by the `Xikolo::API` gateway. It passes through `Xikolo::Versioning::Middleware` for version negotiation based on the `Accept` header, followed by authentication middlewares (`Auth::Middleware::LegacyToken`, `Auth::Middleware::Session`). The request is then routed to the appropriate endpoint within the mounted API version (e.g., `V2::Base`). Any exceptions are caught by `Xikolo::API`'s `rescue_from` block, which converts `Error::Base` exceptions into standardized HTTP Problem Details responses. Responses are formatted using `Format::PrettyJSON` or other defined formatters.

The `Xikolo::API` maintains a list of `Versioning::Version` objects representing supported API versions. When a client makes a request, `Xikolo::Versioning::Middleware` inspects the `Accept` header to determine the client's desired API version. The API responds with the latest compatible minor version. If a client requests a deprecated version, the `Xikolo::Versioning::Middleware` may add a `Sunset` header to the response, informing the client about the upcoming end-of-life for that API version.

The `Xikolo::API` provides a `make_docs!` method that triggers the `Xikolo::Docs::Generator` to create API documentation. This generator processes the definitions within specific API versions, such as `V2::Base`, to produce comprehensive documentation files, typically in a directory like `./doc/api/`.

This workflow encompasses the core operations for managing user accounts, including creation, retrieval, modification (e.g., password changes, confirmation), deletion, and masquerading. These actions are typically performed by administrators or helpdesk agents with appropriate permissions.

This workflow describes how new permissions, roles, and groups are defined and integrated into the system. Definitions are made in YAML files within the `Xikolo::Account` service, and then loaded into the database using a specific Rake task, typically during deployment.

This critical operational workflow is executed when existing permissions, roles, or groups are modified or removed, especially for course-specific groups. It involves generating and executing SQL scripts to ensure that grants are correctly updated or deleted across the database, preventing stale or incorrect permissions from persisting.

This workflow focuses on the management of platform-wide permission groups, such as `xikolo.gdpr_admins` or `xikolo.helpdesk`. It involves defining these groups and their roles, and in specific cases (e.g., removing grants or restructuring groups), performing manual console operations to adjust existing grants.

This workflow enables an external chatbot to interact with the Xikolo platform on behalf of users. It encompasses authenticating the chatbot, then authenticating specific users via SAML UIDs, and subsequently allowing the chatbot to query user-specific data (courses, achievements, quizzes) and perform actions like course enrollment/unenrollment.

This workflow facilitates the exchange of course information between Xikolo and the MOOChub platform. While the specifics of the data exchange (e.g., push, pull, synchronization) are not detailed in the provided context, an API endpoint is exposed for this purpose.

This workflow allows external e-commerce shops to programmatically create and manage digital vouchers for Xikolo products. This includes bulk creation of vouchers and querying the status of existing vouchers (e.g., whether they have been claimed).

This workflow supports an external translation pipeline (TransPipe) by providing structured access to Xikolo's course and video content. This includes fetching course and video metadata, retrieving existing subtitles, and allowing the translation service to upload updated or new subtitles for videos.

When a user interacts with a learning item (visits it or submits a result), the system updates their progress. This involves recording the visit, storing the result, and then recalculating the user's progress for the specific section and the overall course. The final learning evaluation can be dynamic (calculated on-the-fly) or persisted (pre-calculated).

The system provides various API endpoints to retrieve statistics about courses, enrollments, and individual learning items. This includes overall enrollment counts, enrollment trends, and detailed item performance metrics like submissions and average points.

For specific courses, the learning evaluation can be explicitly triggered for recalculation. This is typically an administrative action or a scheduled task to ensure all progress data is up-to-date, especially after significant course structure changes or data migrations.

The Course service provides API endpoints for managing enrollments, including creation, updates (e.g., marking as completed), and deletion. It also exposes detailed enrollment information, including visits, points, and completion status, which can be enriched with learning evaluation data.

Covers the creation, updating, and deletion of courses, including associated metadata, content structure, and external integrations. This workflow ensures that course data is consistent and propagated across the system.
Manages user enrollments in courses, tracks their progress through sections and items, and calculates overall course completion and achievements (CoP/RoA). It also handles course reactivation.

Defines and evaluates prerequisites for courses using course sets and relations. This ensures users meet specific criteria (e.g., Confirmation of Participation or Record of Achievement in other courses) before accessing certain content or enrolling.

A one-time or on-demand process to migrate courses from a legacy structure (where hierarchy is implicit) to a new explicit content tree managed by `Structure` nodes. This enables advanced content management features.

Allows course administrators to set up A/B tests for course content by defining content tests with multiple groups. Users are assigned to groups in a round-robin fashion, and content forks are created for each group.
Covers the creation, retrieval, update, and soft deletion of documents and their localized versions, including file storage and event publishing.
Allows users to search and filter documents based on various criteria such as associated course, item, language, and tags.
Enables the duplication of course-specific visual assets (images, videos, and their subtitles) from one course to another, including S3 file operations and database record management.

Users interact with the Pinboard Service to create, view, update, and delete discussion posts or 'pins'. This workflow involves fetching user and course context from respective services and potentially triggering notifications.

A service publishes an event message to Msgr. The NotificationService, via its consumers, receives and processes this message, leading to the creation of a notification record and triggering email generation.

Following the processing of a notification event, the NotificationService renders a mail template, applies styling using Inky and Foundation, and then inlines CSS with Premailer before sending the final HTML email.
Allows for brand-specific customization of email layouts and stylesheets by placing custom files in designated brand folders within the NotificationService, overriding default templates.

Users (e.g., administrators, course instructors) create, edit, and delete news items, which can be designated as global announcements or specific to a particular course. This workflow involves API interactions with the `Xikolo::NewsService` to persist and manage these items.

Upon creation or update of a news item, the `Xikolo::NewsService` handles its distribution. This can involve making the news accessible via its API for display in the main web application and potentially sending out email notifications to relevant users. Email notifications can be customized per brand.

This workflow involves the TimeEffortService fetching necessary data from CourseService and QuizService to compute and potentially store or expose the estimated time effort for individual course items.
The process of creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting quiz definitions, including questions and their respective answers, within the system.
The workflow encompassing the recording, storage, and initial scoring of user responses to quizzes. This includes handling the lifecycle of a user's attempt at a quiz.

A critical operational workflow for adjusting quiz scores and submission data. This process is initiated when quiz content (questions, answers, points) changes after users have already submitted their answers. It involves executing specific `rake` tasks to modify submission records and recalculate points, followed by an update to the overall course results.

Ensures that all Xikolo applications and services access consistent, environment-aware configuration values. The `xikolo-config` gem manages the loading and merging of configuration from various YAML files, allowing for platform-specific overrides.
involvedComponents: All Xikolo services and the main application

workflows.description: Standardizes the handling of file uploads, storage, and retrieval across the Xikolo ecosystem. Services use the `xikolo-s3` gem to interact with AWS S3, managing their dedicated file spaces, validating uploads, and processing file references within content.
involvedComponents: Services requiring file storage (e.g., CourseService, PinboardService)

workflows.description: The process of initializing the PostgreSQL database schema and applying subsequent changes over time. This workflow involves configuring database connections, executing Active Record migrations, and leveraging custom PostgreSQL features for efficient and robust data management.

The process of populating the database with initial data, typically for development, testing, or initial production setup. This workflow allows for structured and environment-specific data loading, ensuring a consistent state across different environments.
Running a local development server with hot module reloading for efficient frontend development, powered by Webpack Dev Server.
Automated checks for code style, formatting, and linting errors before code is committed to the repository, ensuring consistent code quality.
Automated formatting of various code files (JS, TS, CSS, SCSS, Markdown, Ruby, Slim) using Prettier and other language-specific formatters.
Static analysis of TypeScript code to catch type-related errors before runtime, improving reliability and maintainability.

Starts all necessary Xikolo web application and microservices locally using `overmind` based on the `Procfile` definitions. This workflow enables developers to run and test the entire distributed system on their local machines.

The process of building Docker images for the Xikolo platform, including base images (ruby-base, ruby-base-node, ruby-base-chrome) and individual service images. This workflow uses `docker buildx bake` and respects the `.dockerignore` rules.

Orchestrates and deploys the entire Xikolo platform, including all microservices, the main web application, and supporting infrastructure, using Docker Compose. This workflow ensures all services are built, configured, linked, and started in the correct order.

Configures the web application servers (Puma or Unicorn) for optimal performance and resource management in different environments. This includes setting thread/worker counts, port binding, and managing database/message queue connections during process lifecycle events.

Sets up and migrates the PostgreSQL database for the Xikolo platform. This workflow is critical for preparing the database schema and ensuring all services have a consistent and up-to-date data store.

Loads initial user permissions into the database, typically after database migration. This ensures that the `Xikolo::Account` service and other dependent services have the necessary authorization data available.

Mnemosyne actively extracts full application traces, including cross-application requests, providing detailed performance and execution flow information. Sentry also collects transaction data for performance monitoring, with configurable sampling rates and exclusion of health checks.

Developers can use a Sentry event ID or a Mnemosyne trace ID (found in error pages or Sentry reports) to look up detailed application traces in Mnemosyne. This allows for in-depth analysis of the request flow, including query parameters, across microservices.
The process of starting the Rails application, including loading gems, configuring the Rails environment, and initializing the application instance.
A Rake task-driven workflow to prepare a Continuous Integration environment, involving database setup and asset internationalization export.
The process of precompiling frontend assets, which includes a check to ensure that if a specific brand is set, its corresponding asset directory exists.
A workflow for managing and validating translation keys across different locales, including exporting translations for JavaScript consumption and identifying missing keys.
Users interact with the application in their preferred language, with all static UI elements, messages, and dynamic content rendered according to the active locale.
When a translation key is not found for the active locale, the system gracefully falls back to English or displays a placeholder, ensuring a consistent user experience and aiding debugging.
Backend-defined translations are made available to the JavaScript frontend, allowing dynamic UI components and client-side logic to be localized without duplicating translation efforts.
The application supports loading locale files specific to a particular brand, enabling customization of language resources for different platform instances or white-labeling scenarios.

Content stored in the database with multiple language variants can be dynamically selected and displayed based on the user's locale preferences, ensuring that user-generated or administrative content is also localized.
This workflow describes the process of an authorized user creating or updating a static content page, including handling embedded file uploads and managing translations.
The process of running unit, integration, request, feature, and view tests using the RSpec framework to verify individual components and their interactions.

Running comprehensive, full-stack tests that simulate real user behavior across all microservices and the UI by driving a browser. This workflow ensures critical functionality works from a user's perspective.
Performing static analysis on Ruby code to ensure adherence to predefined style guides, best practices, and to identify potential issues before runtime.

A user (logged-in or anonymous) accesses the helpdesk, describes an issue, provides an email (if anonymous), and submits the ticket. The system verifies reCAPTCHA, creates a ticket record, sends an email to support, and publishes a message to the message queue.

A user accesses the helpdesk, potentially with a course pre-selected, selects a course category, describes an issue, and submits the ticket. The system verifies reCAPTCHA, creates a course-associated ticket, sends a course-prefixed email to support, and publishes a message to the message queue.

Before a helpdesk ticket is processed, the system performs a reCAPTCHA verification. If the initial verification fails, the user may be prompted for manual verification. Ticket creation proceeds only upon successful verification.
Administrators create new voucher codes, often in batches, for specific products or courses, which can then be distributed externally.
A logged-in user enters a voucher code to activate a paid feature (e.g., Proctoring, Reactivation) for a specific course, subject to product prerequisites.
A daily background job automatically anonymizes claimant IP addresses for vouchers claimed more than one year ago to comply with data privacy regulations.
Administrators can search for and view the detailed information of a specific voucher using its code.
Administrators can view aggregated statistics about voucher usage and status.
When a user navigates to the dashboard, an AJAX request is initiated to fetch and display the next available poll for them to interact with. If no poll is available, no content is displayed.

A user selects one or more options for a poll and submits their vote. The system records the response, and then displays a confirmation message, potentially revealing poll results and indicating if another poll is available.

Users can access an archive of past polls. For each poll, the system determines whether to display results based on the poll's status and the user's participation, or provides informational messages if results are not yet available.

As described in the RAG context, this workflow involves a student interacting with a survey item within a course, selecting answers, and submitting the survey. This is conceptually similar to voting on a poll, but likely uses distinct models and potentially different UI components, integrated as a course 'item'.

The system displays a promotional banner on the course list. The `Global::CourseListBanner` component attempts to retrieve the banner from `Rails.cache`. If not found, it queries the `Banner` model for the currently active banner, which is then cached for 30 minutes. The component renders the banner using its image URL, link, and alt text.

The system displays active system alerts to users. The `Navigation::SystemAlerts` component fetches published alerts from the `Alert` model, caching them per language for 5 minutes. It then checks the user's `seen_alerts` cookie to determine which alerts are new and renders them, potentially with a popover for unread messages. User interaction (e.g., opening the alert list) updates the `seen_alerts` cookie.

Administrators create and manage banners using a `rake banner:create` task. This task prompts for banner details, uploads the image to S3 via `Banner.upload!`, and creates a `Banner` record. Deleting a `Banner` record triggers an asynchronous job (`S3FileDeletionJob`) to remove the corresponding S3 object after a delay, accounting for caching. The `Rails.cache` can be manually cleared to force immediate banner updates.

System alerts are created by administrators via the Rails console. An `Alert` record is created with publication and expiry dates, and localized translations (title and text) which support Markdown formatting. The `Alert` model ensures a default translation exists.

This workflow ensures that gem dependencies are consistently versioned across the main application and all microservices. The `check-gem-versions` script automates the process of identifying discrepancies, which is crucial for maintaining a stable and predictable microservice environment.

This workflow describes how application-wide and environment-specific configurations are managed and applied across services. The `xikolo-config` gem centralizes configuration, allowing values to be defined in YAML files and overridden based on the environment and deployment context, ensuring consistent settings like base URLs and branding.

This workflow outlines the process for handling file uploads and managing S3 resources across services. The `xikolo-s3` gem provides the necessary abstractions for interacting with AWS S3, validating uploads, and managing file references within content. It emphasizes a decentralized approach where each service is responsible for its own file space.

This workflow details how background jobs are configured and executed across the application. The `xikolo-sidekiq` gem sets up Sidekiq, integrates with ActiveJob, and manages Redis connections. It also enables the scheduling of periodic tasks using `sidekiq-cron` based on environment-specific configurations.

This workflow describes the process of collecting custom application and engineering metrics from various Ruby-based services. The `xikolo-common` gem provides a standardized interface (`Xikolo.metrics`) to send data to Telegraf, enabling centralized monitoring and analysis in Grafana for performance and operational insights.
The process of compiling and bundling frontend assets for deployment or development. It involves Webpack for modern assets and the Rails Asset Pipeline for legacy assets.
Automated checks performed before a commit is finalized to ensure code quality, style consistency, and type correctness. This workflow is managed by Git hooks.
The process for developers to add new JavaScript or TypeScript code to a specific Webpack bundle.
The standard procedure for integrating new third-party JavaScript libraries or tools into the project's frontend dependencies.
The process for updating the Node.js version used across the project, including local development environments and CI/CD pipelines.

The process of initializing the Rails application, loading configurations, setting up the runtime environment, and preparing the server to handle requests. This includes loading gems, configuring Rails defaults, and applying environment-specific settings.

The process of compiling and bundling frontend assets (JavaScript, CSS) using Webpack and Sprockets, and exporting internationalization data. This workflow supports multiple brands and is crucial for preparing the application's UI.

The multi-stage process of building Docker images for the web application and other services. This includes installing dependencies, compiling assets, and setting up the runtime environment for efficient deployment.
The comprehensive workflow covering user login, session management, permission checks, and feature flag evaluation to control access to application resources and functionalities.

Mobile applications interact with the Xikolo API (mounted at `/api`) to fetch and submit learning-related data. This workflow involves version negotiation using the `Accept` header and handling deprecation notices via the `Sunset` header to ensure client compatibility and guide updates.

workflows.workflowName: Internal Service Integration via Bridge APIs
workflows.description: Various internal services and components integrate with the main application through dedicated 'bridge' APIs (e.g., Transpipe for video, Lanalytics for statistics, Moochub for courses, Chatbot for user interaction, Shop for vouchers). These APIs provide specialized endpoints for specific domain interactions.

External customer portals access and manage data related to courses, users, and enrollments through the dedicated Portal API (`/portalapi-beta`). This provides a controlled interface for external systems to interact with core application data.

workflows.workflowName: API Version Management and Client Updates
workflows.description: The API actively manages different versions to support diverse client bases. Clients declare their supported API version, and the API responds accordingly, including 'Sunset' headers for deprecated versions. This process guides clients, especially mobile apps, to update to newer API versions before older ones are removed.
The process of evolving the database schema over time using ActiveRecord migrations, adhering to best practices for reversibility and performance.
A multi-step process for migrating data between old and new schema structures, designed to ensure data integrity and minimize impact on production systems.
The process of setting up a new database instance and populating it with essential or sample data, configurable for different environments.
The architectural decision and implementation for using UUID v7 as primary keys across the database, leveraging custom PostgreSQL functions.
The strategy to create a pre-joined and denormalized view of complex course data to optimize read performance for common queries.
This workflow describes how application errors are captured and reported to Sentry, including filtering of sensitive data and exclusion of expected exceptions.
This workflow outlines how Mnemosyne captures full application traces and how Sentry error events are linked to these traces using a unique Trace ID, enabling cross-service debugging.

This workflow describes the process for developers to use a Trace ID from a Sentry error to look up the complete application trace in Mnemosyne for detailed debugging, including query parameters and cross-service calls.

Users authenticate through various external identity providers (e.g., SAML, OpenID Connect) configured via OmniAuth. Upon successful authentication, the system either finds an existing user or creates a new one, linking an authorization record to their account. A user session is then established.
involvedComponents: External Identity Providers (e.g., SAML IdP, OpenID Connect Provider)

workflows.description: Users can modify their profile details, such as display name, full name, email address, birthdate, and avatar, directly on their profile page. The frontend JavaScript handles the inline editing UI and sends asynchronous AJAX requests to the backend API to persist these changes in the database.
A user attempts to access course content, and the system verifies their eligibility based on course publication status, start date, user authentication, and enrollment status/permissions.
Users interact with learning items (visit, submit assessments), and the system records their activity and determines if item and section prerequisites are fulfilled based on visits or scores.
Administrators and teachers create, edit, and configure courses, sections, items, metadata, offers, and visual assets through a dynamic frontend interface.
Courses are categorized using classifiers and clusters, enabling filtering, tagging, and highlighting (e.g., featured courses) on the course list and detail pages.
Users can reactivate expired courses, extending their access and submission deadlines, typically requiring vouchers and specific platform/course configurations.
The system automatically calculates, creates, updates, and deletes deadlines for various course resources, ensuring users are informed of upcoming actions.

Courses are grouped into sets, and directed relations between these sets define complex prerequisites for course tracks, requiring specific achievements (e.g., Confirmation of Participation) in preceding courses.
Anonymous or unenrolled users are directed to a featured video item in 'open mode' to provide a preview of course content, enhancing engagement and SEO.

This workflow encompasses the entire lifecycle of a user account, from creation and registration to updates (e.g., password changes, profile edits), and potential deletion or administrative actions like masquerading and manual confirmation.

This workflow describes how user access to platform features and data is controlled. It involves defining permissions, bundling them into roles, assigning roles to groups, and then granting these groups access based on context. This system supports global and course-specific permissions.

This workflow enables platforms to define and manage additional, custom data fields for user profiles. It includes the process of creating these fields (text, select, multi-select), making them mandatory, and handling user input, potentially interrupting user access until mandatory fields are completed.
This workflow encompasses the creation, configuration, and maintenance of quizzes, including their questions and answers. It supports both direct API interaction and bulk import via XML.
This workflow describes the process where a user takes a quiz, submits their answers, and the system processes these submissions, potentially grading them and storing the results.

Content editors create, edit, update, move, and delete quiz questions and their associated answers within a course item. This workflow involves selecting specific question types (e.g., Multiple Choice, Free Text) and defining properties for questions and answers.

A logged-in user initiates a new quiz attempt, interacts with quiz questions, and submits their answers. The system manages time limits, submission deadlines, and proctoring (if enabled). User progress can be auto-saved via snapshots. Upon submission, an event is published to the messaging queue for further processing.
involvedComponents: ACFS Client Models (e.g., Xikolo::Quiz::Quiz, Xikolo::Submission::QuizSubmission, Xikolo::Submission::UserQuizAttempts, Xikolo::Submission::QuizSubmissionSnapshot)

workflows.description: After completing a quiz, users can view their submission, review results, and access historical attempts. The system determines which submission to display (e.g., highest score or newest) and presents the results, including a score, percentage, and a graph of past performance. Users can navigate between different submissions.
involvedComponents: ACFS Client Models (e.g., Xikolo::Quiz::Quiz, Xikolo::Submission::QuizSubmission, Xikolo::Submission::UserQuizAttempts)

workflows.description: An API endpoint allows frontend components to fetch aggregated quiz recap data for a specific course. This data includes questions, answers, and links back to the original course items, enabling a summary view of quizzes.

Users or other services request a list of available courses or detailed information about a specific course. The Course Service filters courses based on visibility and can embed additional data like descriptions or enrollment status.
Users can enroll in or unenroll from a course. This workflow involves creating, updating, or deleting an Enrollment record, reflecting the user's participation status.
The system tracks a user's progress and points within a course to determine eligibility for 'Confirmation of Participation' and 'Record of Achievement' certificates, based on configured thresholds.

When a course is created or a user is assigned a specific role (e.g., teacher, admin) within a course, the system manages the creation of course-specific user groups and grants appropriate permissions.
Users create, read, update, and delete discussion questions, answers, and comments. This workflow involves direct API interactions for content submission and retrieval.
Users interact with discussion content by casting votes (up/down) and subscribing to discussions to receive updates. This involves API calls and potentially asynchronous notifications.
Users can report inappropriate discussion content. This workflow captures abuse reports via the API and likely triggers background processes for review and potential action.
Tasks such as sentiment analysis of new posts, sending notifications for subscribed discussions, or other long-running operations are handled asynchronously to maintain API responsiveness.
Users can view a list of discussion questions (topics) for a course, filter them by tags, and navigate through different sections, including a dedicated 'Technical Issues' section.
Users can create, view, edit, delete, upvote, close, reopen, block, unblock, and report abuse for discussion questions. This workflow also includes accepting an answer for a question.
Users can create, view, edit, update, delete, block, unblock, and report abuse for comments made on questions and answers.
User actions on the pinboard, such as creating questions, answers, comments, accepting answers, and voting, trigger asynchronous events that update user gamification scores.
Administrators create, edit, delete, and view announcements through a dedicated interface. This includes handling multilingual content and managing publication settings.
Administrators can send email notifications for announcements, either as a test or to all recipients. The system tracks and displays email delivery statistics.
A workflow where other microservices publish events to RabbitMQ, which are then consumed by the Notification Service to generate and send corresponding email notifications to users.
The process of dynamically selecting and rendering email content (subjects, body text, links) based on the user's preferred language, using extensive locale files.
A scheduled workflow (likely initiated by Sidekiq cron) that compiles and sends daily administrative and course-specific statistics reports via email.

A user or system creates a new global or course-specific news item via the News API. This action triggers the storage of the news item in the database and potentially publishes a message to RabbitMQ. A Sidekiq job is subsequently enqueued to process and send notifications (e.g., emails) to relevant users, potentially fetching user preferences from the Account service and course context from the Course service.

Users can manage their notification preferences related to news and announcements, including options to unsubscribe from specific types of announcements or all emails globally. Links for these actions are provided within the notification emails. The News Service likely queries the Account service for user notification settings to determine which notifications to send.
Users view videos, interact with the player (seek, pause), and create discussion topics linked to specific video timestamps. Keyboard shortcuts enhance accessibility.
Administrators can add, edit, delete, and view video providers, configuring their credentials and initiating synchronization processes.

workflows.workflowName: Video Item Creation/Update with Attachments and Subtitles
workflows.description: Teachers create or update video items, uploading associated reading materials, slides, transcripts, and subtitles. The system handles S3 storage and subtitle processing.

workflows.workflowName: Video Streaming and HLS Playlist Generation
workflows.description: The system dynamically generates HLS master and stream playlists, incorporating various video qualities and subtitle tracks, optimizing for different devices and bandwidths.
Users can view subtitles for videos, and administrators can upload, update, or delete subtitle files. Subtitles are served as VTT files with appropriate headers.
When enabled, the system generates specific URLs for courses and videos that integrate with the external TransPipe service.
The ability for users to download video and audio content is controlled by a course-specific setting, while supplementary materials like slides and transcripts are always downloadable.

Allows administrators to create, view, edit, and delete PDF certificate templates for a specific course, including uploading PDF backgrounds, defining dynamic content, and previewing the generated certificates.
Enables administrators to create, view, edit, and delete Open Badge templates for a specific course, including uploading PNG badge images and defining badge metadata.
The internal process for generating a PDF certificate from a `Certificate::RecordOfAchievement` and its associated `Certificate::Template`.
The internal process of embedding a signed Open Badge assertion into a PNG image file, creating a 'baked' Open Badge.

Administrators can create, edit, clone, and delete courses. They can manage course channels, classify courses into clusters, and order both channels and classifiers. Document management (a beta feature) and teacher profiles are also administered here. Quiz content can be previewed and imported.

Administrators can view a dashboard with platform-wide and course-specific statistics, including user activity, enrollments, certificate counts, and geographical distribution of learners. This data is often cached for performance.
Enables teachers to create and modify LTI exercises, including setting up rich text instructions that can incorporate S3-hosted files.

This workflow involves the process of determining and storing the estimated time effort for various learning items (e.g., courses, sections, quizzes). It likely involves fetching item details from CourseService and QuizService, applying calculation logic within the TimeEffortService, and persisting the results. This process can be triggered by messages (via MsgrConsumer) or background jobs (via TimeEffortWorker).

This workflow describes how user actions across different services (e.g., Course, Pinboard) lead to the creation of gamification scores. Events are published to RabbitMQ, consumed by the GamificationConsumer, and then processed by specific rule classes to create score records.

This workflow outlines how earned badges are rendered and displayed to the user, typically on a dashboard or achievements page. The Dashboard::GamificationBadge component retrieves badge data and uses asset images to visualize them.
This workflow describes how users progress through different levels based on accumulated experience points (XP) and how their current level and score are displayed in the UI.
involvedComponents: UI (global nav bar, dashboard achievements page)

workflows.description: An external chatbot authenticates a user using a shared SAML `uid` to obtain a temporary user token. This token is then used to retrieve user-specific information (e.g., internal ID, enrolled courses, achievements, quizzes) and manage course enrollments (enroll/unenroll) on behalf of the user.

External shop systems interact with the platform to programmatically create new vouchers (e.g., for course reactivation or proctoring) in bulk. They can also query and list existing vouchers, including their current status (claimed/unclaimed) and associated details.

An external translation pipeline system retrieves course and video metadata from the platform. It can also fetch existing subtitle files (WEBVTT format) for specific videos and languages, and subsequently update or create new subtitle files, optionally marking them as automatically generated.

The platform provides a dedicated API endpoint to facilitate integration with the MOOChub Schema repository. This workflow enables the exchange or synchronization of course-related data with external MOOChub systems, adhering to the MOOChub schema specification.

A user navigates to the helpdesk page, fills out a form with their issue, and submits it. The system verifies the submission, creates a ticket, sends an email notification, and publishes a message queue event.

A logged-in user accesses their personalized dashboard, which aggregates and displays their current, upcoming, and completed courses, promoted content, upcoming dates, and potentially a notice for new SSO users.

An anonymous or logged-in user visits the application's root URL, seeing a public homepage that features announcements and dynamically loaded course categories, topics, or videos based on configuration.
Users can browse a public list of courses, apply filters based on channel, topic (classifier), language, and search queries, with support for pagination to load more courses.
A logged-in user can view a list of their certificates and other relevant documents associated with their completed course enrollments.
If the gamification feature is enabled, a logged-in user can view their achievements and gamification progress on their dashboard.
Describes the process of a user navigating to their preferences page and the system retrieving and displaying their current settings.
Outlines the end-to-end process when a user changes a preference setting, from frontend interaction to backend persistence and event propagation.
A message-driven process to duplicate an existing course, triggered by an event containing the old and new course identifiers.
Updates the state and recipient count of a news item based on messages received, likely from a notification service.
Asynchronously publishes a user's LTI grade to the course service to ensure their progress is accurately reflected.
After a proctored quiz submission, this job fetches the detailed proctoring results from an external vendor and stores them locally for future reference.
Following a proctored quiz, the user's proctoring image is retrieved from the vendor (SMOWL) and uploaded to S3 for inclusion on certificates.
Periodically deletes user accounts that have remained unconfirmed for a specified duration to maintain data hygiene.
A recurring task to remove IP addresses associated with voucher claims, likely for privacy or data retention compliance.
A recurring task to synchronize newly added videos, ensuring content is up-to-date across the platform.
Users can expand and collapse content sections to reveal or hide information. The system ensures that only one section is expanded at a time within a given accordion group.

Users can filter and search content on a page by entering text into a search bar or selecting options from dropdowns. The system provides a clear button to reset the search and dynamically updates the displayed content, often with a loading indicator.
Users can click a UI element (button or icon) to copy associated text to their clipboard. The system provides visual feedback to confirm the copy action.

Users interact with a date/time picker to select specific dates and times. The system supports custom formatting, timezone handling, and provides convenience buttons for common actions like 'Today' or 'Clear'.

Users can navigate through horizontally arranged content (e.g., course cards, topics) using scroll buttons or by directly scrolling. The system dynamically adjusts the visibility of navigation buttons based on content overflow.
Users can dismiss various banners (browser warnings, cookie consents) and system-wide alerts. The system hides the UI element and often records the dismissal via a cookie to prevent repeated display.

Users interact with an interactive transcript displayed alongside a video. They can see the currently spoken text highlighted, automatically scroll the transcript, or click on a transcript cue to jump to that specific point in the video.
Users can access a helpdesk panel by clicking a dedicated button. The system dynamically adjusts the button's appearance and position, and the panel may contain a chatbot or other support options.

This workflow describes how the application determines the active language for a user's request and allows users to change it. It follows a specific priority order to ensure the most relevant locale is applied.
This workflow outlines how localized strings are accessed from the translation data store and then used to render dynamic content in the application's views or within business logic.
This workflow details the process of compiling backend YAML translation files into a JSON format that can be consumed by the frontend JavaScript application, enabling client-side localization.
Administrators create multiple vouchers through a web interface, specifying details like count, tag, associated course, and product type.
External shop systems programmatically create batches of vouchers by sending requests to the Bridge API, specifying quantity, product type, country, and tag.
A logged-in user redeems a voucher code for a specific course product. The system validates the code, checks product prerequisites, and applies the voucher's benefits.

A daily scheduled background job automatically clears the `claimant_ip` field for vouchers that were claimed over a year ago, ensuring compliance with data privacy regulations. [Source: app/jobs/voucher/delete_claimant_ip_job.rb, spec/jobs/voucher/delete_claimant_ip_job_spec.rb]
Administrators can query individual voucher details by code and view aggregated statistics about voucher usage through the admin interface. [Source: app/controllers/admin/vouchers_controller.rb]
External shops can retrieve a list of existing vouchers, with options to filter by tag, claimed status, and claim date ranges, via the Bridge API.
Administrators view platform-wide statistics like user counts, enrollments, and activity. The data is fetched from various microservices and cached for performance.
Administrators or course staff view detailed statistics for a specific course, including geographical data, item visits, and video statistics.
Users with appropriate permissions can view, create, restart, and delete data export report jobs through the admin interface. The frontend polls for job status updates.

A user selects a file (image or general document) via a form. The frontend JavaScript (Dropzone.js) intercepts the upload, uses pre-signed S3 URLs and metadata provided by the backend, and uploads the file directly to S3. The backend then receives a reference to this uploaded file (upload ID or S3 URI) for validation and final processing.

When editing a form with an existing file, the backend provides the file's URL to the frontend. The frontend JavaScript displays this file in the Dropzone preview area. Users can choose to delete the existing file, which triggers a client-side DELETE request to S3 and updates hidden form fields to signal deletion to the backend upon form submission.

After a file is no longer needed (e.g., replaced by a new upload, or associated resource deleted), the backend schedules an asynchronous job to remove the file from S3. This job uses the `xikolo-s3` gem to perform the deletion.

For rich text fields containing embedded file references (e.g., images in a markdown editor), the `Xikolo::S3::TextWithUploadsProcessor` helps manage these files. It tracks changes, commits new uploads, and identifies obsolete files for deletion when the markup content is updated.
External applications can update certain attributes of a user's profile on the openHPI platform or initiate the deletion of a user account. User identification is based on their SAML 2.0 protocol ID.

External applications can interact with user enrollments in courses. This includes retrieving a list of all courses a user is enrolled in (optionally filtered by a specific course) or creating a new enrollment for a user in a designated course.

Users visit the application and are presented with a navigation component that displays system-wide alerts. New alerts are visually highlighted, and users can interact with the component to view details and dismiss alerts, marking them as 'seen'.

Administrators create and manage system-wide alerts, including defining their content (with localization and Markdown support) and publication schedule. This is currently performed via the Rails console.
The application displays a single active banner, typically in a prominent location like a course list. The banner's content, image, and link are determined by the currently active banner record.

Administrators create new banners by providing an image URL, alternative text, and publication/expiry dates. The system handles downloading the image, uploading it to S3, creating the database record, and asynchronously deleting the S3 object when a banner is destroyed.

A user requests a static page, which is retrieved based on locale preferences, rendered from Markdown to HTML, and displayed with S3 URIs converted to public URLs. Administrators can see options to create missing pages.
An administrator edits a static page. The rich text editor handles embedded file uploads to S3. Upon submission, the content and S3 files are processed, and obsolete files are scheduled for deletion.

A teacher creates or updates rich text content for a course item. The system processes the rich text, handles S3 file uploads, and conditionally schedules obsolete files for deletion, ensuring files still referenced elsewhere are preserved.

Captures information about external websites that refer users to the platform. This data is enriched with user and context information, then asynchronously sent to an analytics service for aggregation and reporting.
Manages redirects to external URLs, ensuring the target link is valid and providing an optional interstitial notice page to inform users before redirection, mitigating open redirect vulnerabilities.
Provides dedicated endpoints for direct navigation to specific courses, items, or pinboard entries within the platform. It involves fetching necessary resource details from respective microservices.

Facilitates redirecting users to an external LimeSurvey instance for surveys. It carefully manages query parameters, sanitizing sensitive tracking data, adding required survey parameters, and including a hashed user identifier for authenticated users.
A user encounters a cookie consent banner, makes a decision (accept or decline), and their preference is stored, preventing the banner from reappearing for that specific consent.
